title: Serum Neurofilament Light Chain Is Not an Independent Predictor of Autonomic Neuropathy in Hereditary Transthyretin Amyloidosis
content: Serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) is a biomarker for peripheral neuropathy as sNfL correlates with polyneuropathy severity in hereditary transthyretin (ATTRv) amyloidosis. It is unclear whether sNfL also correlates with autonomic neuropathy. In this study, we aimed to predict the presence of autonomic neuropathy in patients with ATTRv amyloidosis based on sNfL levels. sNfL was measured retrospectively in 10 pathogenic transthyretin gene variant (TTRv) carriers and 28 patients with ATTRv amyloidosis. All 38 individuals underwent a comprehensive evaluation for autonomic neuropathy. Individuals with autonomic neuropathy had a higher median sNfL level compared to those without autonomic neuropathy (p< 0.001). In univariable logistic regression analysis, age-adjusted sNfL status (normal versus abnormal for age) was associated with sex, autonomic neuropathy, and peripheral neuropathy. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, only peripheral neuropathy remained the independent predictor of age-adjusted sNfL status (normal versus abnormal for age). Abnormal age-adjusted sNfL status was associated with autonomic neuropathy, but only peripheral neuropathy independently predicted abnormal sNfL status in TTRv carriers and ATTRv amyloidosis patients.
